static_traits.name: Zhang Rudi
static_traits.family_status: Living with spouse, has two children (one diagnosed with autism), keeps two dogs
static_traits.social_status: Strained relationships with family members; has a supportive spouse, but confides less due to guilt
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no prior psychotherapy history; self-blame and sense of failure markedly worsened after the child's autism diagnosis
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, highly cooperative, overall negative and self-denying tone; frequently using 'should/must' self-demanding statements; anxiety and guilt prominent, highly sensitive to small mistakes

basic_info.main_problem: I often feel I am failing as a mother, especially when I make small mistakes. This sense of failure began after my child was diagnosed with autism.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these feelings of failing as a mother are affecting my mental health and my relationship with my family.
growth_experiences: After the child's autism diagnosis, the client's sense of failure and self-blame markedly worsened, initially attributing the child's condition to herself, with very high stress; since then, whenever a small parenting slip occurs (e.g. forgetting to prepare snacks, missing appointments, waking late), it triggers daily inadequacy and intense self-criticism, gradually affecting the relationship with her spouse as well as daily self-care and life enjoyment.

core_beliefs: I am a useless / incompetent mother

special_situations.event: One day forgetting to wake the child, the child unable to get to school on time
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I haven't arranged everything properly and the child is affected, it means I am a failure mother
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubles self-reproach to push improvement; tightens the day's arrangements and manages the schedule more strictly to make up for mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am the worst mother; I ruined their day

special_situations.event: Forgetting to prepare snacks for the children
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make even one small mistake, it proves I cannot do anything well
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: More organized, strictly follows parenting advice and makes checklists to avoid repeating mistakes

special_situations.event: Misses the child's appointments (such as school- or treatment-related)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the child misses something important, it's all my responsibility, proving I am incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces sharing stress with the spouse or others, bearing it alone to avoid disappointing others
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I disappointed my family,It is all my fault

special_situations.event: When facing challenging parenting situations (especially related to the child's autism)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As a mother I must be perfect at all times and cannot make mistakes
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly demanding myself with high 'should/must' standards, forcing improvement through perfectionism
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should do better; I cannot make mistakes

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be a 'good enough' mother, able to control and protect the children, gaining recognition and peace of mind
core_conflict.fear: Fearing my imperfection will hurt the children and disappoint the family, thus being seen as a failed mother
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of control and improvement through self-harshness and perfectionism
Reduces expressing feelings to my partner to avoid being seen as a burden, maintaining superficial relationship stability

object_relations.object_representation: A child dragged down by me, needing my perfect care

object_relations.self_representation: One who adds burden to others
object_relations.object_representation: A supportive partner who I may exhaust

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests practicing self-compassion and letting go of excessive self-blame
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client believes 'being kind to myself is indulgence and irresponsibility, and will make things worse' (transferentially understanding self-compassion as losing control)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Insists on high standards and 'should' statements, emphasizing the need to be perfect; tone is tense and severe, lists the necessity of self-criticism, and downplays emotional feelings.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When encouraged to communicate more openly with my spouse about my pressure and feelings
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client believes 'I will annoy him and add burden', projecting her own worries as the other's reaction
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expresses worry about boring her partner, hesitant tone, avoids in-depth discussion, instead emphasizing that she should bear it alone to avoid troubling others.

manifestations: Worrying about burdening the partner and reducing confiding
Often bearing parenting pressure alone, hard to obtain connection and support
outcomes: Emotional exhaustion, hard to enjoy life

manifestations: Daily entangled in 'not good enough' self-evaluation, struggling to gain satisfaction from daily activities and self-care
Positive efforts (organizing and following advice) negated by herself

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Frequently using 'should/must' self-demands (e.g. must be perfect, cannot make mistakes)
Turning social/parenting norms into rigid standards for herself without digesting them

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Worries about burdening the partner, so reduces expression and help-seeking
Turning pressure and dissatisfaction into harsh self-criticism and self-punishment

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessive self-criticism and cautiously restraining self-expression
Repressing true feelings for fear of annoying others

positive_force: Has a supportive spouse who can provide emotional support
Willing to seek professional help and try self-compassion practice
Has a certain degree of organization and tries hard to follow parenting advice
negative_force: Negative cognitive patterns such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization, and personalization appear frequently
Perfectionism and self-blame maintained by high standards and 'should' self-demands
Strong sense of guilt; worries about burdening the partner and reduces help-seeking
Repeatedly thinking about small mistakes, hard to relax and enjoy daily life

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive self-blame and rumination over small parenting mistakes (accompanied by anxiety and guilt)
antecedent: Forgetting to wake the child, causing lateness
Forgetting to prepare snacks for the children
target_behavior.core_reason: After the child's autism diagnosis, partially attributing the child's situation to herself, forming the belief 'must be perfect, cannot make mistakes', and catastrophically assessing the consequences of mistakes
target_behavior.function: Maintaining a subjective sense of control and improvement through self-punishment and high standards, trying to avoid repeating mistakes (negative reinforcement); while avoiding facing uncertainty and vulnerability
target_behavior.consequence: Emotional distress worsening, struggling to enjoy daily activities and self-care, tense family relationships

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids expressing genuine stress and emotions to the spouse; reduces help-seeking
antecedent: Worries one's emotions will burden the spouse
Worrying about being disliked or negated by her partner
target_behavior.core_reason: Fear of being seen as a failure and disappointing others, projecting the possibility of negative evaluation onto her partner
target_behavior.function: Avoiding being rejected or judged to maintain superficial relationship harmony (avoiding unwelcome outcomes)
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced social support, increased sense of loneliness, accumulated stress intensifying self-denial
